Answers

Why aren’t people finding my apartment complex online?

Short answer: Renters usually can’t find an apartment community for one of three reasons. Either the property doesn’t show up where renters search, the information they find isn’t convincing, or booking a tour is too hard. Renters search on Google Maps, listing sites, social media and AI tools.

The most common causes

  • You show up when someone types your exact name, but not for searches like “2 bedroom apartments in Scottsdale” or “pet friendly apartments near me.”
  • Your Google Business Profile has the wrong category, missing amenities or old photos.
  • Prices, specials or floor plans don’t match across your website and listing sites.
  • Nearby communities have more recent reviews and more local content than you do.
  • Social media looks good but rarely connects the property to its neighborhood.
  • AI tools like ChatGPT don’t have enough clear facts about your community to recommend it.
  • Reporting shows views and impressions, not calls, tours and applications.

What it costs you

Every renter who doesn’t find you tours a competitor instead, and you pay for that gap in concessions and days on market.

Questions we hear

Is it my website or my Google listing?

Usually both. Renters often decide from Google and listing sites before they ever reach your website.

Do I need more ads?

Not always. Many communities lose renters they could win without extra ad spend in Maps and AI search.

How do I know where I stand today?

A visibility check compares you with nearby communities on the searches renters actually use.
